t:8c658f6d6f48: Jobs, 25, tells Apple's story from the garage to the Apple II: the computer as a "bicycle for the mind", VisiCalc, ease of use, and where personal computing is heading.
t:e8484f0e1cf7: ABC 20/20 interview recorded at Apple's offices on 18 Feb 1981 with reporter Bob Brown, on why personal computers matter. Unedited footage.
t:e16465a77172: Jobs's talk "The Future Isn't What It Used to Be" at the 1983 International Design Conference in Aspen: the history of computers, industrial design, how media evolves, and where Apple is going.
t:2a91330003ee: Apple's full annual shareholders meeting on 24 Jan 1984 at the Flint Center: company business, Apple's history, the "1984" ad, the Macintosh introduction and a Q&A with the Mac team.
t:1fe9ec0d0469: Jobs introduces the Macintosh: the "1984" ad, the Mac speaking for itself, and demos of MacWrite and MacPaint.
t:922abd5e4e8c: At the Apple II Forever event in April 1984, Jobs reports on the Mac's first 100 days, with about 70,000 sold, and shows software written for it.
t:375a3763e3e7: Footage from NeXT's early company retreats: Paul Rand presents the NeXT logo, and the team discusses product and software priorities, deadlines and the college market.
t:05c277a8b273: Jobs's public launch of the NeXT Computer in October 1988.
t:3f43c8e5be60: A long TV interview: the computer as a bicycle for the mind, VisiCalc, desktop publishing, "interpersonal computing", Engelbart and Xerox PARC, the Homebrew Computer Club, the Blue Box and Wozniak.
t:c5ab7a52ee06: Internal video for NeXT employees: Jobs explains target customers, competitors and the go-to-market plan at a whiteboard. He sizes the professional workstation market at about 100,000 units in 1991, with Sun at about 80%.
t:8ef3d2ba304b: July 1991 interview for the 10th anniversary of the IBM PC, probably by Brent Schlender for Fortune: what personal computing achieved in the 1980s and where it goes next.
t:eb71dde38409: Interview recorded on 19 Dec 1991 for a documentary about quality pioneer Joseph Juran: what NeXT learned from him, such as treating work as repeatable processes and measuring how they run.
t:ff5fad1cbb02: Jobs demos Release 3 of the NeXTSTEP operating system.
t:96555e4cd1f1: Talk and Q&A with MIT Sloan MBA students in spring 1992: leaving Apple, NeXT's technology and strategy, portable technology and his management style.
t:a1b0806e2769: A long oral-history interview at 40: childhood and Heathkits, firing underperformers, Microsoft's monopoly and Sculley, Xerox PARC in 1979, the Web, Pixar and Toy Story, and death as life's greatest invention.
t:e2260d3506ca: Robert Cringely's full 1995 interview for the PBS series Triumph of the Nerds, of which only about 10 minutes aired: the Blue Box, building the first Apple, John Sculley and Microsoft.
t:bb6fdff86499: Jobs's SIGGRAPH 1995 keynote on the future of animation: 100 years of film from the Lumière brothers to Star Wars, computer graphics in film, and how Toy Story was made.
t:1ac21ea3b4ed: Radio interview with Terry Gross: the web and HTML, package tracking, dynamic web publishing, e-commerce, WebObjects, direct-to-consumer sales, Xerox PARC, NeXT as a software company, his early Apple years and Apple's culture.
t:7ae14eda806b: Jobs and John Lasseter on The Charlie Rose Show in October 1996, talking about Pixar and the future of animated film.
t:47b10680ccb4: Gil Amelio's Macworld keynote, a week after Apple announced it was buying NeXT. Jobs comes on stage and demos NeXT's OpenStep development tools.
t:4ca0423982a2: An internal Apple staff meeting about eight weeks after his return.
t:8f980f602259: An open Q&A with Apple developers, six months after his return, on his vision for Apple at a difficult time: ending OpenDoc, and starting product decisions from the customer experience rather than the technology.
t:bdd3eb7ad7ba: His first keynote as interim CEO: Apple's new board of directors, a partnership with Microsoft including a $150 million investment, with Bill Gates joining by video link, and a preview of the Think Different campaign.
t:a8fe949099ae: Jobs launches the Power Mac G3, the online Apple Store and build-to-order Macs.
t:7e6d0084c70a: Mac OS 8.1, QuickTime 3.0, and the announcement that Apple has returned to profit, with $45 million expected for the quarter.
t:ec6889cafa82: Jobs presents the four-quadrant product plan (a desktop and a portable each for consumers and pros) and the PowerBook G3, then introduces the iMac, the consumer desktop.
t:ade33d05f9ee: Jobs reports Apple is back on track: inventory turnover, the new distribution system and the online store.
t:758398939507: Jobs announces Mac OS X, combining Mac OS 8 and Rhapsody, and the Carbon API that lets existing Mac apps run on it.
t:eac93e813c05: A third profitable quarter in a row, a 15 August release date for the iMac, the OS roadmap, and a first demo of Mac OS 8.5 and its Sherlock search.
t:a703e8fe4171: A talk to college IT leaders in Seattle: computers in education, net neutrality, thin clients, affordable computing, web portals, TV and role models.
t:f0de72aa3e53: Jobs launches the Blue and White Power Mac G3 and Mac OS X Server, with a demo of 50 iMacs streaming video from one server.
t:8387b6c9fa9b: Jobs's keynote at Macworld Expo Tokyo, recapping January's San Francisco launches, plus the opening of the Apple Store in Japan.
t:57d082c4d16a: QuickTime 4 streaming, the open-source QuickTime Streaming Server and Darwin core, and a preview of Mac OS X Client.
t:8b875f536f04: A speech to employees on the Apple campus.
t:8a75a502cef6: Jobs launches the iBook consumer laptop and AirPort wireless networking, with a live demo of browsing the web without cables, plus QuickTime TV.
t:80c8bb58711e: Mac OS 9 and its nine internet tools, the new iMac line including the iMac DV, and iMovie.
t:369c981add77: The Aqua interface and Quartz graphics engine for Mac OS X, with Mac OS X 10.0 due in January 2001. Jobs also announces he will become full-time CEO.
t:db3f8a8e1ece: Updated laptops and professional desktops, plus an agreement with Dai Nippon Screen to include its Japanese fonts in Mac OS X.
t:c707116cbc79: The iMac DV Special Edition, the Power Mac G4 Cube, three new displays including a 22-inch Cinema Display, and an optical mouse.
t:e33e626c3990: The Paris keynote: the Mac OS X public beta and new iBooks.
t:f4fd9503ac66: The Titanium PowerBook G4, a new Power Mac G4 line with the SuperDrive that burns CDs and DVDs, iTunes and iDVD.
t:4cfc9d4212e0: A new iMac line with CD-RW drives and iTunes, in two new patterns: Blue Dalmatian and Flower Power.
t:617344d4fc71: An event on the Infinite Loop campus: a Mac OS X 10.0 update that adds CD burning, then the new white iBook.
t:c5b11edf8041: Mac OS X Server based on Mac OS X 10.0, and WebObjects 5.
t:06c886e51f30: An update on the new Apple Stores, with 25 planned by the end of the year, faster iMacs and Power Macs, and the features of Mac OS X 10.1.
t:abb633ca1930: The launch of the first iPod.
t:ac1b8f4d1155: The iMac G4 with an LCD screen, a 14-inch iBook and iPhoto.
t:d3de38f6d028: Jobs and Apple's management introduce Xserve, Apple's rack-mounted server for business. Tim Cook's first time on stage for Apple.
t:aa4c28c42d42: Opens with a mock funeral for Mac OS 9, marking the end of its development, then previews Mac OS X 10.2 Jaguar.
t:1ce1195be776: Mac OS X 10.2 Jaguar with iCal, iSync, .Mac and iTunes 3; new iPods including a 20GB model and Windows versions; and a 17-inch iMac G4.
t:70f892e310b4: Mostly a demo of Mac OS X 10.2, plus the announcement of iCal and iSync.
t:23fe179abe02: Two new PowerBooks (12-inch and 17-inch), iMovie, iPhoto, iDVD and iTunes bundled as iLife, the Keynote presentation app and the Safari browser.
t:53992e0551ad: The launch of the iTunes Music Store and new iPods: 200,000 songs from the five major labels at $0.99 each, with no subscription.
t:8cd64cfd4835: At the first D: All Things Digital conference: his plans for the future and his views on the technology landscape.
t:17e96c41abc2: Xcode, the Power Mac G5 and Mac OS X 10.3 Panther.
t:3f827a5a78f5: Updated 17-inch and 12-inch PowerBook G4s, the first aluminium 15-inch PowerBook G4, and a new wireless keyboard and mouse.
t:095b1ae80f3b: iTunes for Windows, iPod accessories, and partnerships with AOL and Pepsi.
t:a2e3087ad9ee: Xserve G5 and Xserve G5 RAID, the iPod mini, and the 10GB iPod raised to 15GB at the same $299 price.
t:ca1525969aef: With iTunes now the biggest legal music download service, he talks about Apple, music and what comes next.
t:7736150cef0f: New Cinema Displays including the 30-inch, and Mac OS X Tiger.
t:6b4f880bea67: Phil Schiller gives the keynote while Jobs is on leave after surgery: the iMac G5, plus an update on the iPod and the iTunes Music Store.
t:5930049788b6: The iPod Photo line and a U2 special edition iPod.
t:0d67743c422a: The iPod shuffle, Mac mini, iLife '05 and iWork. Jobs says Apple sold over 4.5 million iPods in the 2004 holiday quarter and calls 2005 the "year of HD video editing".
t:feea7eb3cb9a: At D: All Things Digital, Jobs demos a new version of iTunes with a podcast directory and one-click subscription, and talks about music, the iPod and phones.
t:5208b88f8446: His speech to Stanford's graduating class on 12 June 2005: three stories from his life about connecting the dots, love and loss, and death. It ends with the Whole Earth Catalog's final message, "Stay Hungry. Stay Foolish."
t:17916d91e68c: Apple will move the Mac from PowerPC to Intel processors, and Wolfram Research talks about porting Mathematica to Intel. Also podcasts in iTunes 4.9.
t:e49178e45ac3: The iPod nano, which replaces the iPod mini, the Motorola ROKR phone with iTunes, and iTunes 5. Also Harry Potter audiobooks on iTunes, and Kanye West performs two songs.
t:42b92a8a79d3: A new iMac G5 with a built-in camera and Photo Booth, and the iPod with video, plus a demo of video podcasts.
t:66b1bac6a377: The first Intel-based iMac and MacBook Pro, iLife '06 and iWork '06, and the first universal version of Mac OS X (10.4.4).
t:3c5c14c54b5f: An Intel-based Mac mini, leather iPod cases and the iPod Hi-Fi speaker system, plus Front Row sharing media between Macs.
t:b3d817005fba: The Mac Pro, which replaces the Power Mac G5, an updated Xserve, Mac OS X Leopard features including 64-bit apps, Time Machine and Boot Camp, and a revised Mac OS X Server.
t:35a8c1b2a17b: Billed as "It's Showtime": Apple TV (code-named iTV), a second-generation iPod nano and a revised iPod shuffle.
t:ce69672d9feb: The iPhone, with Multi-Touch as its interface, in 4GB and 8GB models shipping in the US in June with Cingular. Also Apple TV, and the renaming from Apple Computer to Apple Inc.
t:5c72573bc275: Interviewed by Walt Mossberg at D5 about the iPhone, due in late June, and Apple TV.
t:42b5918f8d64: A demo of the first feature-complete developer beta of Mac OS X Leopard with a redesigned Finder, Safari for Windows, and web apps in Safari as the way to build apps for the iPhone, which ships on 29 June.
t:4122bb2d1256: The first aluminium iMacs, a refreshed Mac mini, and iLife '08 and iWork '08.
t:f7194895e63f: Billed as "The Beat Goes On": the first iPod touch and a third-generation iPod nano. For the iPhone: custom ringtones, the 4GB model dropped and the 8GB cut from $599 to $399.
t:74fcab27a1f9: Software updates for Apple TV, iTunes, the iPhone and the iPod touch; iTunes movie rentals from all the major studios; Time Capsule, Apple's first network storage drive; and the MacBook Air, thin enough to fit in a manila envelope.
t:a2c906713976: The iPhone SDK, Exchange support for business users, and the App Store, where developers set the price and keep 70% of sales. Kleiner Perkins announces a $100 million iFund for iPhone apps.
t:7f5b09972999: The iPhone 3G, iPhone OS 2 and the App Store, plus MobileMe, which replaces .Mac and syncs multiple devices.
t:9466436c3cd2: Recorded on 7 August 2008 with WSJ reporter Nick Wingfield, a month after the App Store opened: over 60 million apps downloaded and about $30 million in sales in the first month, and the App Store's role for the iPhone compared to iTunes for the iPod.
t:0ccc816ac7da: The event of 14 October 2008 introducing the new aluminium unibody MacBook and MacBook Pro.
t:18b5c4611590: Phil Schiller gives the keynote while Jobs recovers from illness: iLife '09, iWork '09 with the iWork.com beta, the 17-inch MacBook Pro, and iTunes songs without DRM.
t:478b8f231a06: Mac OS X 10.6 Snow Leopard, iPhone OS 3 and the iPhone 3GS, with the iPhone 3G cut to $99 on contract.
t:eb32cdca556c: Jobs announces the iPad on 27 January 2010 at the Yerba Buena Center for the Arts in San Francisco.
t:164a9f9cca41: A long interview with Walt Mossberg and Kara Swisher: Flash, Google, the iPad and the missing iPhone prototype. On whether tablets will replace PCs: "PCs are going to be like trucks."
t:8f2725e54767: The iPhone 4 with Retina display and HD video recording, iPhone OS 4 renamed iOS 4, FaceTime, and iMovie for iPhone 4.
t:7318b975851f: A press conference on the iPhone 4's antenna problem: Apple's data, and a free case for every iPhone 4 bought through 30 September, or a refund for anyone who already bought a Bumper.
t:e8d33ce01a73: A new iPod shuffle, an iPod nano with multi-touch, an iPod touch with FaceTime and Retina display, iTunes 10 with the Ping music social network, iOS 4.1 and 4.2, and a new Apple TV.
t:3a4326c73676: The "Back to the Mac" event: iLife '11 with updated iPhoto, iMovie and GarageBand.
t:912b34d7b914: His last keynote: Mac OS X Lion, sold only through the Mac App Store for $29.99, a preview of iOS 5, and iCloud.
t:4dc2dce58d55: The iPhone 4S with an A5 chip, faster graphics and the Siri voice assistant.
t:d6db7a2e8694: Apple's employee memorial on its Cupertino campus on 19 October 2011: speeches from Tim Cook, Bill Campbell, Al Gore and Jony Ive, and performances by Norah Jones and Coldplay.
t:89732593b39c: A fourth-generation iPad with the Lightning connector, a 13-inch MacBook Pro with Retina display, and the 7.9-inch iPad mini.
